hero.name: Dr Yang Bong
hero.role: Senior Lecturer, School of Business and Law
hero.bio: My research brings together digital technologies, participatory research and business. As a Senior Lecturer in the School of Business and Law at Birmingham Newman University, I study digital inclusion, Indigenous entrepreneurship, platform economies and AI for good.

about.heading: About
paragraphs: The work combines fieldwork and community co-design with machine learning and data analytics to study inequality and sustainable development. I also helped found the [Asia-Europe for AI (AE4AI) Network](https://www.asiaeurope4ai.org/) and now coordinate it and its AI for Sustainable Development working group.

Before entering academia, I spent eight years in international marketing and business development. I completed my [PhD in Digital Economy](https://repository.nottingham.ac.uk/handle/123456789/73641) at the University of Nottingham through the Horizon Centre for Doctoral Training.

impact.heading: Impact

items.title: Horizon CDT impact project
items.text: This Horizon CDT impact project, which I secured and delivered, co-designed digital marketing and market-access activities with rural and Indigenous micro-entrepreneurs in Malaysia. Working with the Lun Bawang community of Long Semadoh in rural Lawas, Sarawak, and with the creative agency The Culture Capital, the project grew from digital marketing training into a village-wide branding campaign shaped by community leaders and entrepreneurs.

link.label: Read about the project at Horizon CDT

items.title: Strategic priorities for UK agricultural research infrastructure
items.text: Funded by the ESRC through the Innovation Research Caucus, this study asked where the UK should invest in agricultural research infrastructure. It analysed £1.2 billion of funding across 2,131 projects, alongside a national infrastructure directory, a survey of 604 stakeholders, and interviews and workshops. The report sets out four investment propositions (Preserve, Predict, Ground and Connect). My part included classifying the UK’s agricultural research projects by research theme and type of intervention, using rule-based and AI-assisted text classification, and analysing the stakeholder survey.

project.heading: Long Semadoh, Sarawak
project.summary: In the Lun Bawang highlands of Lawas, the project brought together village leaders, local micro-entrepreneurs and The Culture Capital to co-design a village-wide brand, so that the community could tell its own story to visitors and buyers.
project.quoteNote: The campaign’s tagline invites visitors who truly want to come, while keeping numbers manageable for the village.
outputs: Instagram and Facebook accounts designed for the community to run
Product packaging with a QR code linking to those accounts
Videos, photographs and community interviews for future marketing
A branding and digital marketing workshop for ten micro-entrepreneurs, taught in Malay

feature.label: Featured
feature.heading: Co-organising ASEFInnoLab7
text: The seventh ASEF Higher Education InnoLab asked what role universities should play in advancing AI for good. It was co-organised with the Asia-Europe Foundation (ASEF), the University of Nottingham and Fudan University, with sessions hosted at the University of Nottingham.
Participants worked in teams on white papers, which were launched at Murdoch University, Perth, in November 2026.
